title: Vaginal discharge and pelvic inflammatory disease: syndromic management (India)
specialty: Obstetrics and Gynaecology / Dermatology and Venereology / Primary Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Syndromic management of vaginal discharge (vaginitis and cervicitis) and lower abdominal pain due to pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) in women in India, using NACO colour-coded STI kits, the NACO STI/RTI guidelines and the CDC 2021 PID guideline for regimen duration and inpatient treatment.
findings: Causative organisms (bacterial vaginosis, Trichomonas, Candida; gonorrhoea and chlamydia for cervicitis; anaerobes for PID) from NACO Table 3.2; gonorrhoea and chlamydia doses from NACO Table 3.3.

Kit 2 (green: secnidazole 2 g with fluconazole 150 mg), Kit 1 (grey: cefixime 400 mg with azithromycin 1 g for cervicitis) and Kit 6 (yellow: cefixime 400 mg once with metronidazole 400 mg and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, 28 tablets each) from the NACO kit specifications (2023).

PID diagnostic criteria, 14-day duration, ceftriaxone 500 mg IM outpatient, ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily with doxycycline and metronidazole 500 mg inpatient, admission criteria, 72-hour review, partner treatment and IUD guidance from the CDC 2021 STI guideline.
unverifiedSections: The Kit 6 label duration was not legible; 14 days is from the tablet count and the CDC guideline.
NACO vaginal discharge and PID flowcharts were not in the opened text.
Treatment in pregnancy (doxycycline contraindicated) is general practice; the NACO pregnancy alternatives could not be read.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Vaginal discharge is one of the commonest reasons women in India attend primary care and Suraksha clinics. Most is vaginitis — bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis or candidiasis — treated with Kit 2. Cervicitis from gonorrhoea or chlamydia is less common but causes PID, infertility and ectopic pregnancy, so women with risk factors or mucopurulent cervical discharge also get Kit 1 cover. Lower abdominal pain with cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness is treated presumptively as PID (Kit 6) once ectopic pregnancy and surgical causes are excluded. Partner treatment, HIV and syphilis testing, and follow-up at 72 hours for PID are part of care.
keyMechanisms: Loss of vaginal lactobacilli leads to bacterial vaginosis; Trichomonas is sexually transmitted; Candida overgrows with antibiotics, diabetes or pregnancy.
Gonorrhoea and chlamydia infect the cervix and ascend to the endometrium and tubes (PID).
Tubal scarring after PID causes infertility, ectopic pregnancy and chronic pain.

physicalSigns: Thin grey fishy discharge (BV); frothy yellow-green (Trichomonas); curdy white (Candida)
Cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness (CDC)
redFlags: Missed period or positive pregnancy test with pain: exclude ectopic pregnancy

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Pelvic or lower abdominal pain with cervical motion, uterine or adnexal tenderness, no other cause.
Temperature above 38.3°C, mucopurulent discharge, raised ESR or CRP, positive gonorrhoea or chlamydia.
Surgical emergency not excluded, tubo-ovarian abscess, pregnancy, severe illness or vomiting, temperature above 38.5°C, failure of oral therapy.

clinicalManagement.title: Vaginal discharge
actions: Cervicitis or risk factors: also treat gonorrhoea and chlamydia (NACO).

clinicalManagement.title: Lower abdominal pain
actions: Mild–moderate PID: outpatient regimen (Kit 6 or CDC) for 14 days.

clinicalManagement.title: Partners and IUD
actions: Treat partners from the previous 60 days (NACO; CDC).
IUD need not be removed; consider removal if no improvement in 48–72 hours (CDC).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: Review PID at 72 hours; switch to IV if not better (CDC).
Retest at 3 months after gonorrhoea or chlamydia (CDC).

adjustments: Paediatric: Adolescent girls treated as adults; STI in a child needs child-protection assessment.

CKD: No adjustment.
CLD: Caution in severe liver disease.
Kit 2 (green) also contains fluconazole 150 mg.

teaching.scope: Vaginal discharge and PID in Indian primary care.

PID: low threshold; 14 days of doxycycline plus metronidazole with a cephalosporin.
